4 And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. 5 But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him. (Luke 12:4-5 KJV)

This verse tells us that we should be more concerned about our souls than our physical bodies. For the born again Christian, who obeys Jesus (Hebrews 5:9), has the assurance that upon death of our bodies, our souls will get to go and be with the Lord (Ephesians 1:6), so dying is not something that we should be afraid of (1 Corinthians 15:55). It only makes sense to fear the one who can affect our eternal lives, rather than one who can only kill the body. If you think about eternity, and living forever, then that becomes much more important than our short life on this earth.

The word fear can mean different things depending on its use. Many times when the word fear is used in “fearing God”, it has the meaning of reverencing rather than being afraid of. Reverencing God is something that all believers should do, but we should not ever have a “being afraid of” fear of God (if born again and obeying Jesus), as we are His children, and know that He has a supreme love for us, and will not shed His wrath on His children (Romans 5:9). If you are not born again, then you should be afraid of God and His wrath, as it is directed toward you as an unrepentant sinner. I believe I would much rather be in God’s love than His wrath. The Christian should reverence God all the time, by continually praising and worshiping Him (Psalms 100:4). He is our Heavenly Father, and certainly deserves all our love and worship. Praise You Father!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
